newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladeshis return from UAE with lost dreams.
newsitem.headline: Bangladeshis return from UAE with lost dreams.

text.p: Rafiq Miah arrived at Dhaka airport from Abu Dhabi on Tuesday with only one shirt in a plastic bag and 400 dirhams (US$110) in his pocket.
"This is what I could bring home," said Miah who worked in the United Arab Emirates for seven years as an unlicensed construction contractor.

"I left almost everything back in Abu Dhabi. I could not pay 200 Bangladeshi workers for the last one month because local builders did not pay my dues," he told Reuters soon after he was flown in by a Qatar Airways special flight.
"I could not press anyone for my dues because they knew I did not have a license. Often they threatened to call police," said Miah, overtaken by dispair.
"I have left behind about 200,000 dirhams ($54,500) in unpaid bills against supplies of construction materials."
Looking for a taxi to drive him to his home in northeastern district of Sylhet, 350 km (217 miles) from Dhaka, Miah said: "My dreams have been shattered, but my wife and children are waiting for me."
Miah was one of several hundred Bangladeshis who flew to Dhaka on Tuesday in a desperate bid to escape a new immigration law in the Emirates.
The new law, which comes into effect on October 1, imposes stiff penalties on aliens staying or working illegally in the UAE.

Bangladesh Foreign Minister Abdus Samd Azad said on Saturday that nearly 30,000 Bangladeshis working in the UAE without valid permits or who overstayed would be required to return home under the new immigration law.
He said the government had no plan to compensate the returnees.
Returnee Hossain Ahmed, a middle-aged man who had been working as construction labourer in an Abu Dhabi suburb, had a similar story. So did his nephew Zahidul Islam.
They returned almost empty handed from the oil-rich Gulf state, and said they did not know how they were going to begin life afresh.
Bangladesh airline Biman and foreign carriers had brought back some 6,200 Bangladeshis from the UAE by 32 flights between Thursday and Monday, government officials said.
"People are just fighting for a ticket home", said Aslam Uddin, who had worked in a tailor's shop in Abu Dhabi.
